answer: Running 156 aliases as a result means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden legitimate agents do not face at scale. Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the atlas schedule in the ledge ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the cedar checkpoint releases it only after review. Payout is withheld until peer review closes 5 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. That is 14 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
